findings.title: Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing
findings.body: With enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0, the code runs queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django raises AssertionError('Negative indexing is not supported.') for negative slice bounds, so a user-supplied cursor such as 'x:-5:0' becomes a 500 error. The comment claiming the ORM 'properly handles negative slicing' is wrong. Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, so this is user-controllable. If a negative-stop slice were somehow accepted it could also expose rows outside the intended page, and the 'permissions checked at queryset level' comment does not make this safe.

findings.title: Base BasePaginator now allows negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.body: The shared BasePaginator.get_result was changed so that for is_prev cursors start_offset = offset without clamping to 0. This affects every endpoint using BasePaginator, not just the audit log. A crafted prev cursor with a negative offset now reaches queryset slicing and raises an AssertionError (500). Previously the negative offset hit the same slice, so the max(0, ...) only helps non-prev cursors, and the change is a pointless, misleading edit to shared code.

findings.title: Authorization check may fail and is loosely gated
findings.body: organization_context.member can be None (e.g. for superusers who are not members), so organization_context.member.has_global_access raises AttributeError. Because `or` short-circuits only when the user is a superuser, non-superuser access with no member could also break. The check is also evaluated eagerly for every request, even without optimized_pagination. The optimized path is opt-in via a query param and unlocks the unsafe negative-offset behavior.

findings.title: New paginator duplicates BasePaginator logic with no tests
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator copies BasePaginator.get_result almost verbatim, and get_item_key does not handle datetimes (it calls math.floor on a datetime value, which raises TypeError). The endpoint orders by -datetime, so the optimized path crashes with a TypeError whenever results exist. No tests were added for it.
